commands.stdout:
List local and remote migrations

Usage:
  supabase migration list [flags]

Flags:
      --db-url string     Lists migrations of the database specified by the connection string (must be percent-encoded).
  -h, --help              help for list
      --linked            Lists migrations applied to the linked project. (default true)
      --local             Lists migrations applied to the local database.
  -p, --password string   Password to your remote Postgres database.

Global Flags:
      --create-ticket                                  create a support ticket for any CLI error
      --debug                                          output debug logs to stderr
      --dns-resolver [ native | https ]                lookup domain names using the specified resolver (default native)
      --experimental                                   enable experimental features
      --network-id string                              use the specified docker network instead of a generated one
  -o, --output [ env | pretty | json | toml | yaml ]   output format of status variables (default pretty)
      --profile string                                 use a specific profile for connecting to Supabase API (default "supabase")
      --workdir string                                 path to a Supabase project directory
      --yes                                            answer yes to all prompts

commands.stdout:
Manage Postgres databases

Usage:
  supabase db [command]

Available Commands:
  diff        Diffs the local database for schema changes
  dump        Dumps data or schemas from the remote database
  lint        Checks local database for typing error
  pull        Pull schema from the remote database
  push        Push new migrations to the remote database
  reset       Resets the local database to current migrations
  start       Starts local Postgres database

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for db

Global Flags:
      --create-ticket                                  create a support ticket for any CLI error
      --debug                                          output debug logs to stderr
      --dns-resolver [ native | https ]                lookup domain names using the specified resolver (default native)
      --experimental                                   enable experimental features
      --network-id string                              use the specified docker network instead of a generated one
  -o, --output [ env | pretty | json | toml | yaml ]   output format of status variables (default pretty)
      --profile string                                 use a specific profile for connecting to Supabase API (default "supabase")
      --workdir string                                 path to a Supabase project directory
      --yes                                            answer yes to all prompts

Use "supabase db [command] --help" for more information about a command.

DESCRIPTION
  List local migration files and the migration history of the target database.

TARGET
  Local by default. Pass --remote for the linked project, or --remote=<ref|branch|url>.

USAGE
  supabase migration list [flags]

FLAGS
  --remote[=<ref|branch|url>]    Target a remote database: the linked project, or --remote=<ref|branch|url>.
  --password, -p string          Database password for the project selected with --remote. Not used for the local database or a database URL.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --help, -h                                                          Show help information
  --version, -v                                                       Show version information
  --wizard                                                            Start wizard mode for a command
  --completions <bash|zsh|fish|sh>                                    Print shell completion script (choices: bash, zsh, fish, sh)
  --log-level <all|trace|debug|info|warn|warning|error|fatal|none>    Sets the minimum log level (choices: all, trace, debug, info, warn, warning, error, fatal, none)
  --output-format choice                                              Output format: text (default), json, or stream-json (NDJSON) (choices: text, json, stream-json)
  --output, -o choice                                                 output format of status variables (choices: env, pretty, json, toml, yaml, table, csv)
  --profile string                                                    use a specific profile for connecting to Supabase API
  --debug                                                             output debug logs to stderr
  --workdir string                                                    path to the directory containing your supabase/ folder; used exactly as given, with no ancestor directory search (defaults to searching upward from the current directory)
  --experimental                                                      enable experimental features
  --network-id string                                                 use the specified docker network instead of a generated one
  --yes                                                               answer yes to all prompts; hosted changes only accept this flag or SUPABASE_YES exported in your shell, never supabase/.env or another .env file
  --dns-resolver choice                                               lookup domain names using the specified resolver (choices: native, https)
  --agent choice                                                      Override agent detection: yes, no, or auto (default auto) (choices: auto, yes, no)

PERMISSIONS
  Scoped access token:
    May be required (with --remote, without --password):
      database_write
    May be required (with --remote):
      database_pooling_config_read
      projects_read
    May be required:
      branching_development_read for a preview branch
        or branching_production_read for the main branch
    Optional, with --remote, without --password (command still runs without these):
      database_network_bans_read
      database_network_bans_write
    Optional, with --remote (command still runs without these):
      project_admin_read

DESCRIPTION
  Compares the supabase/migrations baseline with the complete declarative schema tree and writes the difference as migration files. When a legacy export omits known implicit extensions, interactive sync can add declarations and re-plan before writing. Use --no-apply for non-interactive generation without changing the local database; --apply or global --yes applies locally and updates local migration history.

TARGET
  Local only.

USAGE
  supabase db schema declarative sync [flags]

FLAGS
  --no-cache             Disable catalog cache and force fresh shadow database setup.
  --strict-coverage      Fail when bundled pg-delta finds schema objects it cannot manage instead of leaving them unmanaged.
  --schema, -s string    Comma separated list of schema to include.
  --file, -f string      Saves schema diff to a new migration file.
  --name string          Name for the generated migration file.
  --apply                Apply the generated migration to the local database without prompting.
  --no-apply             Generate the migration file without prompting or applying it to the local database.
